I am farming rice here in Mwanza, and this plot of 0.85 hectares is one of my better pieces of land near the lowland where water collects in the rainy season. I cannot afford much chemical fertilizer this year, but I will buy a little urea to topdress when the rice is tillering — maybe one bag for this plot, because without some nitrogen the yield is poor. I use local seed that I kept from last season; the improved seed from the agro-dealer is expensive and I am not sure it suits our water. I depend on the rains and the natural flooding of the lowland, so I do not irrigate with pumps, and my wife and older son help me with the weeding and bird-scaring, but I will hire a few young men for transplanting and harvest because that work is too heavy to finish alone.
